name: Kayla bin-Kroog
title: The Queen Who Endured
role: Yotian noble, queen, and historical chronicler
summary: A royal figure whose life was transformed by Urza's war with Mishra, and whose leadership helped preserve her people after catastrophe.
biography: Kayla bin-Kroog belonged to the ruling family of Yotia. Her marriage to Urza connected the artificer to Yotian political power, placing her close to the origins and escalation of the Brothers' War.

The destruction of Kroog devastated the world Kayla had known. She survived the attack and became a leader for people displaced by the war, facing political and humanitarian consequences that neither brother's inventions could solve.

Kayla's experiences continued beyond the final battle on Argoth. As the climate deteriorated and surviving communities struggled to adapt, she worked to preserve order and protect the people under her care.

Her account, The Antiquities War, became an important historical record of the conflict. Her perspective preserved not simply the actions of Urza and Mishra but the suffering and resilience of those who lived through their decisions.

Kayla's political life began in Yotia, where her connection to Urza linked a ruling family to a powerful artificer. That alliance gave the war a domestic dimension that accounts focused only on battles between brothers can obscure. A ruler's spouse had to confront the practical consequences of campaigns fought in the name of distant strategic goals.

After Kroog fell, survival became a continuing responsibility rather than the end of her story. The later defense of Penregon, retold in The Brothers' War retrospective fiction, shows Kayla evaluating threats as a leader who has already lost a capital. She is especially wary of decisions that treat civilians as expendable parts of another general's strategy.

Her role as a chronicler also demands attention to perspective. The Antiquities War is indispensable for reconstructing how the brothers' rivalry affected Terisiare, but it is a testimony shaped by loss, memory, and the difficult work of governing after catastrophe. Later readers can use her account without assuming it is a view from nowhere.

featuredCard.significance: A depiction of Kayla as a leader whose role continued beyond the military conflict between Urza and Mishra.

source.title: Wizards of the Coast — The Brothers' War, Episode 1: The End
